records.question: What's Delta's policy on oversold flights?
records.ideal_answer: Delta overbooks flights because some passengers with confirmed reservations do not show up, so it may sell more tickets than there are seats. When this results in an oversold flight, Delta first asks for volunteers to give up their seats in exchange for compensation; only if there are not enough volunteers will it involuntarily deny boarding, following the boarding priority rules in Rule 20.
records.answer:
If a flight is oversold, meaning Delta may not have enough seats for all passengers with confirmed reservations, Delta may deny boarding to passengers with confirmed reservations according to this rule [1].

Before denying boarding to any passenger on an oversold flight, Delta will first ask other passengers if they are willing to voluntarily give up their seat in exchange for compensation, which amount and form Delta determines alone [1]. If enough volunteers agree to give up seats based on Delta's offer, then no passenger with a confirmed reservation will be involuntarily denied boarding due to the oversale of the flight [1].

If not enough passengers volunteer to give up their seats after Delta makes an offer, Delta may involuntarily deny boarding to one or more passengers on the oversold flight following specific boarding priority rules [1]:
*   Passengers holding tickets for travel in Premium Cabin, and SkyMiles members with a Diamond Medallion (“DM”), Platinum Medallion (“PM”), or Gold Medallion (“GM”) elite-status designation, as well as passengers with tickets bought under a DL corporate travel agreement [1].
*   Passengers holding tickets for confirmed space in the First or Business class cabin, and SkyMiles members identified with a DM, PM, or G [1].

records.question: Can I get a refund on a non-refundable Delta ticket?
records.ideal_answer: Generally no. Most Delta tickets are nonrefundable and Delta will not refund a nonrefundable fare except where required by law or expressly stated in the Contract of Carriage. If you cancel before departure, the value of the unused portion (less applicable charges) may be applied toward future travel on Delta, and must be used within one year of the original ticket issue date. An exception applies if the passenger dies before travel, in which case the ticket is refunded to the estate on request.

records.question: What are the rules for shipping cargo domestically with Delta?
records.ideal_answer: Delta's U.S.-Domestic Shipping Rules & Tariffs govern cargo moving between points served by Delta within the United States, and between the U.S.A. and points in Canada, as well as transportation performed jointly with other carriers under applicable joint rates. Transportation is subject to the rules, regulations and charges in effect on the date the shipment is accepted by the originating carrier.

*   **Application of Tariff:** The published rules, regulations, and charges apply to transportation between points served within the United States by Delta (the carrier) and also for transport between points in the U.S.A. and points in Canada [1].
*   **Rate Applicability:** Transportation is subject to the rules, regulations, and charges that are in effect on the date a shipment is accepted for transportation from the originating carrier [1]. *   **Acceptable Property:** Property can only be transported if the shipper, consignee, and owner (as applicable) have complied with all laws, ordinances, governmental rules, and regulations governing transportation thereof, as well as all rules and regulations of the tariffs [4].

    *   Live warm-blooded animals will be accepted for transport either as a "Standard" product or as "DASH," which is considered a premium product, up to 100 pounds [4].

    *   Live wild birds require specific conditions for transport: either the shipper or agent must certify in writing on the shipper's letterhead (which must accompany the air waybill) that the birds were born or bred in captivity at special farms, OR the shipment must be between a zoo, sanctuary, preserve, government wildlife agency, or rehabilitation center, AND transportation must be restricted to Delta on-line service [4].
    *   Pug and snub nosed breeds are refused tender if the temperature during any part of their journey exceeds 75 degrees Fahrenheit/ 24 degrees Celsius. Examples include Boston Terrier, Brussels Griffin, Dutch Pug, Japanese Spaniel (Japanese Chin), Japanese Pug, Pekingese, Shih Tzu, and Staffordshire Bull Terrier [4].

    *   Newspapers shipped without an air waybill [3].
    *   All live dogs and cats going into Hawaii [3].

Personal effects include, but are not limited to, wearing apparel, cosmetics, toilet articles, and articles worn by an individual used not for resale [3].

records.question: What are the packaging requirements for shipping cargo with Delta?
records.ideal_answer: Shipments must be packed to ensure safe transportation with ordinary care in handling. Articles susceptible to damage must be adequately protected by proper packing and marked or labelled appropriately. Each piece must be legibly and durably marked with the shipper's and consignee's name and address. Pieces over floor-bearing limits must be secured to a suitable skid or base, liquids and fragile or perishable articles may not be packed with wearing apparel, and hazardous materials must comply with IATA dangerous goods regulations.

records.question: How are fractions of a pound handled when Delta computes cargo weight?
records.ideal_answer: Fractions of a pound are rounded up to the next higher pound, and fractions of a kilogram are rounded up to the next higher half kilogram.
records.answer:
Fractions of a pound will be rounded up to the next higher pound when calculating charges [1]. For computing transportation charges, any fraction of less than one half cent will be dropped, and fractions of one half cent or more will be rounded up to the next higher cent [1].

Additionally, for weight verification, if there is a difference between the weight on the air waybill and the weight shown on the carrier’s scales, the carrier may use the weight from its scales to recalculate freight charges at its discretion [2].
contexts:
Disposition of Fractions
A. Fractions of a pound will be rounded up to the next higher pound. Fractions of a
kilogram will be rounded up to the next higher half kilogram.
B. In computing charges, fractions of less than one half cent will be dropped and
fractions of one half cent or more will be rounded up to the next higher cent.
C. Before computing cubic dimensions:
1. Fractions of less than one half inch will be dropped and fractions of one half
inch or more will be rounded up to the next higher inch.
2. Fractions of less than one half centimeter will be dropped and fractions of
one half centimeter or more will be considered as on centimeter.

Computation of Days
Unless otherwise provided, in computing time in days, full calendar days shall be used
and Sundays and legal Holidays shall be included, except when the last day falls on a
Sunday or legal Holiday in which event the next following calendar day (other than a
Sunday or legal Holiday) shall be included.

Description of Shipments
A. The contents of shipments must be indicated by accurate and specific descriptions
on the air waybill.
B. The number of pieces included in a shipment must be specified on the air waybill.
C. When shipments contain live animals the number of such animals must be
specified by the shipper on the air waybill.

Charges for Weight
A. Transportation charges will be assessed on the gross weight of the shipment based
on the greater of the actual weight or the cubic dimensional weight.
B. Cubic measurement will be based on the greatest dimensions, height, width and
length of the shipment on the basis of 1 pound for each 194 cubic inches or
fraction thereof. Shipments are subject to dimensionalization either at point of
tender or destination and subject to recalculation of freight charges if
dimensionalization is applicable. Note - Shipment dimensions are required on all
bulk air waybills due to enhanced security requirements. Shipment dimensions
must be included in the nature and quantity of goods box on the master air
waybill. Failure to comply may delay acceptance and or movement of shipment.
C. For the purpose of weight verification, all freight tendered to the carrier is subject
to reweighing at either the point of tender or destination. If there is a discrepancy
between the weights shown on the air waybill, as entered by the shipper or its
agent and the weight as shown on the carrier’s scales, shipper and its agent agree
that the carrier, in its sole discretion, may use the weight shown on the carrier’s
scales to recalculate freight charges, the shipper or its agent will be notified by the
carrier of a credit, if weight measured by the carrier’s scales is less than weight
entered on the air waybill by the shipper or its agent. If the weight as measured
by the carrier is more than the weight noted on the air waybill by the shipper or
agent, the shipper or its agent shall be invoiced for the additional charge resulting
from the corrected weight.

Availability of Equipment and Space
A. The carrier will transport all shipments consistent with its capacity to carry and
subject to the availability of equipment of the size and type capable of
handling such shipments.

1. Passenger Baggage 2. Air Mail
3. Small Package (DASH)
4. Standard.
C. The carrier will determine on a reasonable and non-discriminatory basis, the
priority for carriage between shipments and shall decide which shipments shall
not be carried on a particular flight and which shall be removed at any time or
place.

Applicable Rates and Charges
A. Delta's local rates and charges are applicable on all shipments accepted by Delta
except on those shipments where Delta has agreed to provide transportation
jointly with other carriers.
B. All shipments are subject to the rates and charges published and in effect on the
date a shipment is accepted by Delta.
C. When two or more rates, subject to different minimum quantities are provided on
the same commodity in the same shipping form, from and to the same points over
the same route, the lower of the two charges specified under 1 and 2 below shall
be applied:
1. The charge computed on the quantity shipped at the rate applicable to
such quantity, or
2. The charge computed on the next greater quantity for which a lower rate
is provided at the rate applicable to such greater quantity.
D. Unless a higher service is specifically requested by the shipper or mandated by
tariff (I.E. Live Warm-blooded Animals, Articles of Extraordinary Value), all
shipments will be rated as Standard.
E. Except as otherwise provided, when a local or joint rate is established for
application over a particular route from point of origin to point of destination for a
specific service, such rate is applicable over such route, notwithstanding that it is
higher or lower than the aggregate of intermediate rates over such route for such
service.

A. A shipment shall have a value of $0.50 per pound (but not less than
$50.00) unless a higher value is declared on the air waybill at the time of
tendered by the shipper. When a higher value is so declared, an
additional transportation charge of $1.50 shall be required for each
$100.00 (or fraction thereof) by which such higher value exceeds $0.50
per pound. EXCEPTION: (Applicable to shipments of perishables and live

$1.75 per each USD $100.00/CAD $100.00 or fraction thereof, will be

$0.50/CAD $0.50 per pound allowance. Except as noted below, the weight
used to determine the declared value of a shipment shall be the same as

shipment, provided that when a shipment moves on one air waybill over
the lines of one or more carriers at a combination of rates, the declared
value shall be based on the lowest weight upon which charges are based
for any portion of the movement.
B. A shipment moving on one air waybill over the lines of two or more

Charges for Mixed Shipments
